transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, honestly, I'm here because my sleep has just gotten completely unreliable. It's like... even when I go to bed totally exhausted, I just lie there replaying sales forecasts and team issues in my head. And then, if I do fall asleep, I'll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and I just can't get my brain to power down again. It's really starting to get to me.
How long has this pattern of trouble sleeping and racing thoughts at night been going on?
It's been building for a while now. I'd say it really started right around the time our sales division went through a reorganization... so that was about thirteen months ago.
Besides work-related concerns, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life too—like your health, finances, or family—even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Yeah, it definitely spills over. Most days, my mind just... jumps around. I'll start off stressing over whether we'll hit our launch numbers or if someone on my team is about to quit, and then it just shifts right over to the mortgage, or a client renewal. It really feels like every small delay could just turn into something major, even when there's no real reason to panic about it.
Along with the worry and sleep trouble, have you noticed things like muscle tension, feeling restless or on edge, or being more irritable than usual during the day?

Yeah, I definitely do. I just feel... wound up almost all the time. It's like I'm sitting in a stressful pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And the muscle tension is definitely there, too. My shoulders just stay tight pretty much all day, no matter how much I try to relax them.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a persistent low or sad mood, or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you'd normally enjoy?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I don't feel sad or down, just... really stressed and tired from all the worrying. I still want to do the things I normally enjoy, like going out with friends or just watching a movie. It's sometimes hard to fully relax when I'm doing them because my mind is still going, but the actual interest is definitely still there. I'm not feeling depressed, just anxious.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or dizziness, that came on abruptly and peaked within minutes?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I don't get those sudden bursts of panic or anything where my heart is racing out of nowhere. It's more just this constant, steady level of stress and worry all day, rather than a sudden attack.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with chronic (13-month), excessive, and uncontrollable worry spanning multiple domains (work, finances, family), accompanied by sleep disturbance (difficulty falling and staying asleep), muscle tension, and subjective restlessness/feeling on edge. No depressive symptoms (mood/interest preserved), no discrete panic attacks, and no clear adjustment-related stressor confined to a single event—rather, pervasive multi-domain worry consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). Panic Disorder and Adjustment Disorder were considered but excluded due to absence of panic attacks and the diffuse, longstanding nature of the worry beyond a single stressor's adjustment period.
